# Explain DockLayouts panes as ordinary Neo components

## Context

The original fourth series part was explicitly “Panes Are Ordinary Components.” That outcome never received a ticket. The current Adoption guide shows pane resolution, but the refactor and flagship integrations now expose much richer identity, lifecycle, data, and state-provider questions.

## The Problem

Developers can mistake a dock pane for a special docking widget or recreate normal Neo component patterns inside the layout model. There is no focused guide showing how ordinary containers, grids, stores, models, controllers, state providers, async destruction, and stable component identity participate in docking and survive movement.

## The Architectural Reality

Dock documents own semantic pane ids, while consumers resolve those ids into ordinary Neo component instances. `Workspace.mjs` and consumer hooks govern resolution/recreation; stores/providers/controllers retain their own authorities. Moving, pinning, maximizing, or tearing out a pane changes embodiment, not the pane's application-domain identity.

## The Fix

Create `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsPanes.md`: an adopter-facing guide that builds realistic panes from ordinary Neo UI/data primitives and follows their identity and lifecycle across DockLayouts operations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The guide clears the full guide-authoring bar: source/tool-grounded narrative, reader-owned benefits, lived maintainer voice, and at least one render-verified `flowchart TD`.
- [ ] The guide separates explanation from reference: no inlined API/schema/test catalog, and no ticket or PR ids in guide prose.
- [ ] The new source guide is registered in `learn/tree.json` and the SEO `PRIORITIES` input; generated sitemap/LLM outputs remain untouched.
- [ ] Current-source consistency, guide lint, tree lint, portal rendering, and an independent cross-family whole-guide review are recorded in the PR.
- [ ] Examples use ordinary Neo components backed by `data.Store` / `data.Model` where data UI is involved, with providers at appropriate view roots.
- [ ] The guide traces pane identity, component lifecycle, controller/store/provider ownership, destruction, and recreation without moving application state into the dock document.
- [ ] At least one realistic pane is moved through multiple embodiments while its intended state/identity invariants are observed.
- [ ] Generic component, data, and lifecycle reference is linked rather than re-taught.

## Out of Scope

Inventing a pane framework, changing component lifecycle, or embedding app-specific business logic.

## Avoided Traps

Do not hand-map data arrays, put providers into every pane, equate pane id with DOM id, or promise instance preservation where host policy permits recreation.

## Activation Gate

Do not author the guide while #17836 remains an active refactoring authority. At pickup, re-run Memory Core mining, read the current ADR 0029 and source/test surfaces named below, exercise the relevant live subsystem, and revalidate the proposed guide boundary. If the final API makes this split wrong, reshape this ticket before writing—do not preserve a stale outline.
